content.comment_body: I purchased [product_name] [version_no] (Single Licence) and installed it on my desktop running Windows XP, which I use for program development. Everything works smoothly. I installed it on my laptop (also XP) for accessing [product_name] at client sites. The only way for [product_name] to work without freezing is to keep the CD in the laptop. Does this mean I need to buy another [version_no] to use on my laptop?

Hello, It's been around eight years since I last programmed with [product_name]. I've never needed to keep the CD in my PC. Try reinstalling the software with a full installation; it should resolve the issue. Alternatively, if you're short on time, you can use virtual CD-ROM software available online.
Is there any pop-up appearing regarding the license? If not, try reinstalling [product_name] [version_no] and see if it runs properly.

Go to your PC's network and sharing center, select local area connection, then properties. Double-click IPv4 and choose to obtain an IP address automatically, and also opt for automatic DNS server address assignment. Click OK. Attached picture may help. This should resolve the connection problem; if issues remain, try running network diagnostics on your PC.
An original [product_name] CD comes with its license. You can install it on multiple PCs or notebooks. For each computer, install directly from the CD using a complete installation.

Hi, Ensure you have administrator rights, as each PC may have different security settings. Try running the software from the DVD with "Run as Admin." If that works, your issue is likely related to admin rights. Hope this helps.
Thanks for all the suggestions. The real issue was my Java version was outdated. After updating Java, my connection and freezing problems disappeared.

analysis.insight_summary: Users discussed issues with software freezing and needing the installation CD to run on laptops, leading to questions about licensing requirements. The root cause was identified as an outdated Java version rather than a problem with installation or licensing. The conversation also touched on topics of software installation completeness, device permissions, and dependency management affecting usability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the software to work reliably on multiple devices without requiring a CD to be present, and a clear explanation of license constraints. They also hope the software runs smoothly, free of freezes or underlying dependency issues.
